Not in a “I can prove it in court” kind of way, but certain enough that I can’t just brush it off anymore.\n\nShe says the late meetings and the wording in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and I know workplaces can be odd—honestly, in schools, people send the strangest emails at the strangest times. But this has been going on for about a year, and the timing and little changes line up too precisely. It feels like there’s something in them, like a private signal meant for me, something she won’t say directly.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your wife is definitely sending you hidden messages?\n\nPatient: Definitely is a strong word… I mean, I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office things. And maybe in some offices they are—when I was at the school, people would send the oddest emails at ridiculous times, so I get that.\n\nBut this has been going on about a year, and the way the timing and wording line up… it feels too precise to be accidental. So, yes, I do think there’s a private signal in them, something meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t just say outright.\n\nDoctor: If clear proof showed that these messages were just ordinary work messages, would you be able to accept that?\n\nPatient: I mean… if it were really clear proof, I’d want to accept it. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. I’ve worked in education, so I know messages can look strange for no real reason—people send things at odd times, wording changes, all of that.\n\nBut with my wife, it’s been going on for about a year, and it’s the way the late meetings and the little shifts in her work messages line up. It just feels too precise to be nothing. So even if someone showed me proof, I think part of me would still wonder if there was something private in it, like she was trying to tell me something without saying it directly.\n\nDoctor: If your wife showed you a clear, ordinary explanation for one of these messages, would you still believe it was a hidden signal for you?\n\nPatient: If she showed me something really clear for one message, I’d probably say, “All right, that one makes sense.” I don’t want to ignore an ordinary explanation just to be difficult.\n\nBut… the thing is, it’s not just one message. It’s been about a year of late meetings and little changes in how her work messages are worded, and the timing of them—well, it lines up in a way that’s hard for me to chalk up to normal office stuff. I mean, schools have strange schedules too, so I know work can look odd from the outside. But with this, I’d still wonder if there was something underneath it, like a private signal meant for me, something she won’t say directly.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?\n\nPatient: Hearing voices? I don’t think so… not like someone speaking when the room is empty. I mean, sometimes a house makes noises, or you think you hear your name because of a TV in the next room or something—when I worked at school, the hallways were like that, always sounding like someone was calling from somewhere.\n\nBut no, I haven’t really noticed voices talking to me when no one’s there.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that outside events, like TV shows, radio, or people talking nearby, are sending special messages meant specifically for you?\n\nPatient: Not TV or radio so much… I mean, I don’t sit there watching the news thinking they’re talking to me. Sometimes people say things nearby and it catches my attention, but that happens to everyone, especially if you’ve worked in a school—you hear half a conversation in a hallway and your brain fills in the rest.\n\nThe thing I keep coming back to is my wife’s work messages. She says the late meetings and the wording changes are just normal office stuff, and maybe in a regular situation I’d believe that. But for about a year now, the timing has lined up too neatly. It feels like there’s something private in it, like a signal meant for me, telling me something she won’t just say directly.\n\nDoctor: Apart from your wife’s messages and meetings, do you believe anyone else is trying to send you hidden messages?\n\nPatient: Not really anyone else, no. I mean, sometimes you notice patterns in things, like at school when the bell schedule changes and everybody acts like it’s no big deal, but you can tell something’s going on behind the scenes… sorry, that’s probably not what you mean.\n\nIt’s mainly my wife’s work messages and the late meetings. She says it’s just normal office stuff, and maybe some of it is, but for the past year the timing and the little wording changes have lined up too neatly. It feels like there’s a private signal in there, meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your wife is having an affair?\n\nPatient: I don’t want to say it like I have proof, because then people act like you’re accusing someone, and that’s not… I mean, I worked in a school, you learn how quickly rumors can turn into something official just because someone says it the wrong way.\n\nBut yes, I worry that something is going on. My wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and maybe some of it is. But for about a year now it’s lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It feels like there’s a private signal in there, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t just say directly.\n\nDoctor: Before this started with your wife, did you generally tend to distrust other people and suspect they had hidden motives?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I wouldn’t have put it that way. I mean, in a school you learn not to take everything at face value—people say one thing in the staff room and then something else gets decided in a meeting, and suddenly everyone acts like it was obvious all along.\n\nBut generally? I don’t think I walked around assuming people had hidden motives. I tried to be careful with people, sure. Maybe I noticed things other people didn’t always notice. But this with my wife feels different than just ordinary caution.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: No, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest exactly. I still go in for my teaching sections, and I keep up with the data analysis stuff. I ride my bike when I can, too—actually the route by the park is better now than it used to be, except people don’t signal on the path, which drives me a bit mad.\n\nAnd I still meet friends for chess. So it’s not like I’ve stopped doing things. The main trouble is more at home, when my wife and I get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. That can take the enjoyment out of the evening, but I haven’t stopped wanting to see people or do my usual things.\n\nDoctor: Has anyone told you that your speech or your thoughts seem hard to follow or don’t make sense?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure, really. I mean, people have told me I get a bit detailed when I explain things—my wife says I “circle around” before getting to the point, but that’s also because if you leave out the context people misunderstand you.\n\nAt school, actually, that used to happen with lesson plans. Someone would ask a simple question, but if you didn’t mention the timetable or which student group you meant, the answer sounded wrong. So I suppose I can be thorough.\n\nBut hard to follow? Not that I can think of. No one has sat me down and said my thoughts don’t make sense, if that’s what you mean.\n\nDoctor: Have people said that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to?\n\nPatient: Emotionally flat? I’m not sure anyone’s said that, no. My wife might say I get quiet, but that’s not the same thing, is it? I mean, lots of people get quiet when they’re tired or when the conversation keeps going in circles.\n\nAt work I think I’m pretty much the same. The students can tell if you’re bored with a lesson, so you have to be a bit animated, otherwise the whole room just sort of sinks. I don’t think anyone’s told me I seem less expressive, not in those words anyway.\n\nDoctor: What do you think your wife is trying to tell you through these messages?\n\nPatient: I think she’s trying to tell me something without saying it outright. I know she says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, but they’ve been lining up too precisely for about a year now.\n\nIt’s like... not a code exactly, but a private signal. That’s what it feels like.\n\nDoctor: Before this started with your wife, did you often suspect that people were trying to deceive or take advantage of you?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so, not generally. I was probably careful, maybe a bit particular about facts and wording, but I didn’t go around thinking everyone was trying to take advantage of me. I mean, thoughts come into your head all the time, don’t they? Like when you’re marking papers and suddenly remember you left the laundry in, or a student says one word and it reminds you of a song from twenty years ago.\n\nBut someone controlling them? Putting them there? No, I wouldn’t put it that way. My thoughts feel like mine, even if sometimes I turn things over too much.\n\nDoctor: Did this start suddenly, over a few days?\n\nPatient: No, not over a few days.
